summary: Abrupt 5xx wave: HTTP/2 stream resets at API gateway + runtime watchdog restarts
description: Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-10 12:10 UTC multiple enterprise tenants reported elevated 5xx rates for short-lived requests to the text-generation endpoint. Impact: sustained 5xx rate reached ~12% for 20 minutes for some tenants (MapleHealth notably). Environment: prod us-west; API Gateway + HTTP/2 frontend to serving-runtime. Observed: rapid stream resets at the API gateway (HTTP/2 RST_STREAM with error code 0x1) coincident with multiple serving-runtime watchdog-triggered process restarts. Expected: graceful draining with retries limited by backoff; 5xx should be <0.1%.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Send a burst of short streaming requests (concurrency 300, average request body 400B) to /v1/chat/stream on prod-us-west simulated tenant
2) Observe API gateway metrics for HTTP/2 stream resets and per-connection stream counts
3) Correlate with runtime /proc logs for watchdog restarts and OOM/fatal signals
4) Attempt a controlled warmup of runtime pool with persistent long-lived connections to reproduce prefetch/backpressure behavior
observed_behavior: API gateway shows spikes in HTTP/2 RST_STREAM events and per-connection stream saturation
Serving runtime processes hit watchdog timeout, degrade, and are restarted by sidecar supervisor
Client sees 502/503/504 responses depending on where reset occurred; retries amplify load and cause additional restarts
expected_behavior: API gateway should queue/slow-down requests rather than preemptively resetting streams
Serving runtime should shed load gracefully (429 + retry-after) rather than restart under transient backpressure
logs: 2026-03-10T12:12:07Z runtime[worker-7] WATCHDOG timeout: no heartbeat for 45s, sending SIGKILL pid=34721
metrics: api gateway request rate: baseline 2.1k r/s -> burst 4.6k r/s
runtime process restarts: 0/min -> 6/min during incident window
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: sudden request burst causing API GW HTTP/2 stream window exhaustion -> stream resets -> runtime receives partial frames and watchdogs due to stalled KV prefetch I/O
Checked node-level memory: no consistent out-of-memory at kernel level; individual processes killed with SIGKILL (137) observed after watchdog timeouts

Observed pattern: short-lived requests (small payload) with aggressive client retry policy caused many half-open streams; API GW limited active streams per conn and sent RST_STREAM rather than queueing
Reproduced locally with traffic replay (concurrency 300, retries=3) produced same RST_STREAM pattern and runtime restart cascade
Related to earlier issue SUP-661234 (apigw-vpc-peering-signal-loss) only in that both show increased stream churn; root cause differs (this is resource saturation + watchdog sensitivity)
actions_taken: Applied temporary mitigation at 12:30 UTC: reduced API gateway max concurrent streams per connection from 100 to 50 and enabled queueing to avoid RST_STREAM on backpressure
Increased runtime watchdog heartbeat timeout from 45s -> 90s as immediate safety to avoid restart storms
Throttled aggressive tenant-level clients (MapleHealth) to their committed rate via per-tenant token bucket for 30 minutes
Opened runtime follow-up PR to add graceful-backoff (https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2431)
Notified MapleHealth support contact and provided workaround guidance (reduce client retries, exponential backoff)
Scheduled full root cause runbook and post-incident review
next_steps: 1) Postmortem meeting scheduled 2026-03-13 16:00 UTC with SRE, Runtime, and API Gateway owners
2) Implement runtime prefetch queue backpressure and non-fatal error handling in v2.3.2 (target 2026-03-20)
3) Update API Gateway to prefer HTTP/2 GOAWAY/REFUSE_STREAM semantics rather than RST_STREAM for overloaded connections
4) Add synthetic test covering short-request high-retry patterns in canary suite
5) Clean up per-tenant throttling rules and convert temporary blocks into opt-in limits
comments: 2026-03-10T12:45Z - Ravi Kapoor (assignee): Started triage. Correlating api-gateway RSTs with runtime watchdogs. Working on a short-term mitigation (increase watchdog timeout).

2026-03-10T13:10Z - Sophie Chen (reporter): Customer (MapleHealth) confirms partial restoration of service after throttling applied. They reported spike coincided with a scheduled batch job and aggressive retries from their client library.
2026-03-10T14:02Z - Lina Torres (SRE): Applied api-gateway config change to enable queueing and lower per-connection streams. Observed 5xx drop to ~1.2% over 15 minutes.
2026-03-11T09:15Z - DevEx (engineer): Created runtime PR to add softer watchdog behavior and metrics for blocked prefetch ops (see related_github_prs).
resolution: Partial mitigation applied (gateway queueing + extended watchdog). Full fix planned in runtime v2.3.2 to improve prefetch backpressure handling. Customer follow-up scheduled. Marking incident for postmortem and long-term fixes.
